direction: This records the change type for the decision in D010, which was saved with the default REFINE_SCOPE label: the question itself changed from mechanism efficacy ('does adding a temporal relevance term improve accuracy?') to measurement ('what version-level point-in-time failure rates do existing retrievers exhibit, and does valid-time gating reduce them where recency decay does not?'). The direction, hypothesis and supporting evidence are those of D010 and are not restated here; no new scope reduction is introduced.
hypothesis: Existing retrievers, including the published recency-decay hybrid, exhibit measurable version-level point-in-time failures on amended legal text with near-duplicate successive clause versions, concentrated on queries whose in-force version is not the latest, and valid-time gating reduces those failures where decay does not.
rationale: Recorded for taxonomic accuracy so the change of research question, not merely a scope refinement, is visible in the investigation history; the underlying evidence is the convergence of D010's comparisons.
research_question: What version-level point-in-time retrieval failure rates (selection of superseded or not-yet-in-force clause versions) do sparse, dense and hybrid retrievers - including the published lexical+dense+recency-decay hybrid - exhibit on continuously amended legal text with near-duplicate successive clause versions, and does valid-time (as-of) gating reduce those failures where recency decay does not?
